title: Virtual Browser and API Access authoritative glossary

records.definition: General allocator evidence that a job may execute on a particular node under exact policy/capability/capacity generations; not an API egress reservation.
Explicit reservable/releasable outbound route/session selected by API Client for a particular operation; distinct from job placement.
Long-lived web-application state containing semantic document/origin/cookie/storage/checkpoint state; distinct from placement and network sessions.
Short-lived read-side authority for an observer/subscriber; grants visibility but never terminal/browser control.
Declarative hard outbound constraints such as country, VPN, network, egress class and required tags.
Deterministic non-rasterised projection of document/application state for humans or AI, compatible with the terminal-shaped Observation surface.
Browser/API behaviour that suppresses unnecessary resources and respects rate, burst, polling and remote-service limits.
Amount-of-work accounting/admission dimension; priority and desired WLU/second are separate concepts.
Reference to attributable capability/policy evidence. It is evidence linkage, not a bearer capability.
Monotonic identity for an advertised capability state used to detect stale/equivocating placement or egress evidence.
Semantic state revision produced by a terminal/browser observer; distinct from observation stream sequence.
Ordering of detached records in an Observation stream; distinct from engine generation and Queue Fabric delivery identity.
Exceptional placement/runtime capability for sites that genuinely require a real rendering/browser engine; not the default Virtual Browser path.
